chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, who said:

I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام: What is the limit of the water with which the deceased is washed, just as they have narrated that the junub performs ghusl with six arṭāl and the menstruating woman with nine arṭāl? So is there a set limit for the deceased regarding the water with which he is washed?
So he عليه السلام wrote: The limit of washing the deceased is that he should be washed until he becomes pure, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

key_terms.أَرْطَالٍ: ratls, a unit of measure for quantity
key_terms.الْجُنُبَ: a person in a state requiring ghusl due to janabah
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: the water used for ritual washing

ai.seo_question: Is there a fixed amount of water required for washing the deceased in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the fiqh ruling concerning the amount of water used for ghusl of the deceased. The reply states that there is no fixed measured quantity; rather, the deceased is to be washed until purification is achieved.
